problem_markdown: Determine all real polynomials $P(x,y)$ homogeneous of some positive integer degree $n$, with $P(1,0)=1$, such that $P(b+c,a)+P(c+a,b)+P(a+b,c)=0$ for all real $a,b,c$.
solutions_markdown:
The solutions are $P(x,y)=(x+y)^{n-1}(x-2y)$ for every integer $n\ge1$.

Put $g(t)=P(1-t,t)$. Substitution of $(a,b,c)=(t,1-t,0)$ gives $g(t)+g(1-t)+1=0$. Using $(a,b,c)=(u,v,1-u-v)$ and this identity yields $g(u+v)=g(u)+g(v)-1$. Therefore the polynomial $f=g-1$ is additive. Comparing coefficients in $f(2t)=2f(t)$ forces $f(t)=ct$. Also $g(0)=1$ and the first identity gives $g(1)=-2$, so $c=-3$.

For $x+y\ne0$, homogeneity now gives $P(x,y)=(x+y)^n g(y/(x+y))=(x+y)^{n-1}(x-2y)$. Polynomial continuity extends this to $x+y=0$. Direct substitution verifies the displayed family.
